name: The Shunammite woman
charge: Constraining the man of God to eat bread; building him a little chamber on the wall, with a bed, a table, a stool, and a candlestick
summary: A great woman of Shunem noticed that a holy man of God passed by continually and made him a room. She asked nothing. She was given a son; when he died on her knees she laid him on the prophet's bed, saddled the ass, and said, It is well. He was raised. Years later, back from a famine, she got her whole house and land restored by the king in one morning.
offense: She said unto her husband, Behold now, I perceive that this is an holy man of God, which passeth by us continually. Let us make a little chamber, I pray thee, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick. Asked what could be done for her, she answered, I dwell among mine own people. When the child was dead she said to her husband and to Gehazi, It is well, and did not stop until she caught the prophet by the feet.
judgment: About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son. And the woman conceived, and bare a son at that season. The child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes; and Elisha said, Take up thy son. Then she went in, and fell at his feet, and bowed herself to the ground, and took up her son. After seven years' famine she came to cry to the king for her house and land at the very moment Gehazi was telling him how Elisha had restored a dead body to life; and the king appointed an officer: Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.

entries.commentary: A certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cries to Elisha that her husband is dead, that her husband feared the Lord, and that the creditor has come to take her two sons to be bondmen. Because the husband died in debt, the creditor comes to take the sons to work off what is owed. Elisha asks what she has in the house, and she says nothing but a pot of oil. He tells her to borrow empty vessels from all her neighbors, not a few, then shut the door upon herself and her sons and pour oil into all the vessels. She pours out, and the oil continues until every vessel is full, and only then does the oil stay. Elisha tells her to sell the oil, pay her debt, and live with her children on the rest. The empty vessels she borrowed from her people, the children of Israel, were filled through the spirit of the Lord.

Elisha passes through Shunem, where a great woman constrains him to eat bread, and as often as he passes by he turns in there to eat. She perceives that he is a holy man of God and tells her husband to make a little chamber on the wall with a bed, a table, a stool, and a candlestick, so he may turn in whenever he comes. On a day when he rests in the chamber, Elisha wants to bless her and sends Gehazi to ask what may be done for her, whether she would be spoken for to the king or the captain of the host. She answers that she dwells among her own people. Gehazi tells Elisha the woman has no child and her husband is old. Elisha tells her that about this season, according to the time of life, she shall embrace a son. Like our mother Sarah, she does not believe it and tells the man of God not to lie to his handmaid, yet she conceives and bears a son at that season. -

When the child is grown, he goes out to his father to the reapers and cries, my head, my head. His father has a lad carry him to his mother, and he sits on her knees till noon and then dies, from what seemed only a headache. She carries the child up and lays him on the bed of the man of God, the bed in the chamber she had made for Elisha, shuts the door, and goes out. She calls to her husband for a young man and an ass so she may run to the man of God, and though he asks why, since it is neither new moon nor sabbath, she answers, it shall be well. She rides to Elisha at Carmel, and when the man of God sees her afar off, he sends Gehazi to ask whether it is well with her, her husband, and the child, and she answers, it is well.

When she comes to Elisha at the hill, she catches him by the feet, and Gehazi comes near to thrust her away, but the man of God says let her alone, for her soul is vexed within her and the Lord has hid it from him. She says, did I desire a son of my lord, did I not say do not deceive me. Elisha tells Gehazi to gird up his loins, take his staff, greet no man on the way, and lay the staff on the face of the child. The mother says, as the Lord liveth and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee, so Elisha rises and follows her. Gehazi goes on before them and lays the staff on the face of the child, but there is neither voice nor hearing. He returns to tell Elisha the child is not awake.

When Elisha comes to the house, the child is dead, laid upon his bed. He goes in, shuts the door upon them both, and prays to the Lord. He goes up and lies upon the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands, and stretches himself upon the child, and the flesh of the child grows warm. He walks in the house to and fro, goes up and stretches himself upon him again, and the child sneezes seven times and opens his eyes. Elisha calls Gehazi to call the Shunammite, and when she comes he tells her to take up her son. She falls at his feet, bows to the ground, takes up her son, and goes out. This is another act of the Most High through Elisha, restoring the child to life.

Elisha comes again to Gilgal, where there is a dearth in the land, and the sons of the prophets sit before him. He tells his servant to set on the great pot and seethe pottage for them. One goes out into the field to gather herbs, finds a wild vine, and gathers his lap full of wild gourds, shredding them into the pot, for they knew them not. As the men eat, they cry out, O thou man of God, there is death in the pot, and they cannot eat. Elisha tells them to bring meal, casts it into the pot, and says pour out for the people that they may eat, and there is no harm in the pot. He cures the poisoned food so the men may eat safely.

A man comes from Baal-shalisha and brings the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley and full ears of corn in the husk. Elisha says, give to the people that they may eat. His servant asks how he should set this before a hundred men, but Elisha says again, give to the people, for thus saith the Lord, they shall eat and shall leave thereof. He sets it before them, and they eat and leave some, according to the word of the Lord.

Elisha warns the Shunammite woman whose son he restored to flee the coming seven year famine, and she sojourns in the land of the Philistines. When she returns to appeal to the king for her house and land, Gehazi is at that moment telling the king how Elisha restored a dead body to life. The timing is of the Most High, so the king restores all that was hers and the fruits of the field from the day she left.

Ben-hadad king of Syria, sick, sends Hazael to inquire of Elisha whether he will recover, for the word of a prophet, also called a seer, was precious in those days. Elisha tells Hazael the king may recover but the Most High has shown that he shall surely die, then weeps because he sees the evil Hazael will do to Israel: burning strongholds, slaying young men, and ripping up women with child. Elisha tells Hazael he will be king over Syria, revealing that leadership can discern spirits at work in a man that the man does not see in himself. Hazael returns and smothers the king with a wet cloth and reigns in his place.

Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife. He does evil in the sight of the Most High, yet Judah is not destroyed for David his servant's sake, according to the promise.

In Jehoram's days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah and makes a king over itself, breaking the subjection Edom had been under from the days of David and Solomon. This revolt fulfills the word spoken to Esau, that when he gained the dominion he would break the yoke from off his neck, a pattern reaching to Edom's later rise. Jehoram sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place. -

Ahaziah son of Jehoram begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the house of Ahab, being the son-in-law of that house, a picture of the generational curse passed from father to son. He goes with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria, and the Syrians wound Jehoram at Ramah. Jehoram returns to Jezreel to be healed, and Ahaziah goes down to see him, setting the stage for both kings to meet Jehu's judgment.

And she said unto her husband, Behold now, I perceive that this is an holy man of God, which passeth by us continually.

Let us make a little chamber, I pray thee, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall be, when he cometh to us, that he shall turn in thither.
And it fell on a day, that he came thither, and he turned into the chamber, and lay there.
And he said to Gehazi his servant, Call this Shunammite. And when he had called her, she stood before him.

And he said unto him, Say now unto her, Behold, thou hast been careful for us with all this care; what is to be done for thee? wouldest thou be spoken for to the king, or to the captain of the host? And she answered, I dwell among mine own people.
And he said, What then is to be done for her? And Gehazi answered, Verily she hath no child, and her husband is old.
And he said, Call her. And when he had called her, she stood in the door.
And he said, About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son. And she said, Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid.
And the woman conceived, and bare a son at that season that Elisha had said unto her, according to the time of life.
And when the child was grown, it fell on a day, that he went out to his father to the reapers.
And he said unto his father, My head, my head. And he said to a lad, Carry him to his mother.
And when he had taken him, and brought him to his mother, he sat on her knees till noon, and then died.
And she went up, and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut the door upon him, and went out.
And she called unto her husband, and said, Send me, I pray thee, one of the young men, and one of the asses, that I may run to the man of God, and come again.
And he said, Wherefore wilt thou go to him to day? it is neither new moon, nor sabbath. And she said, It shall be well.
Then she saddled an ass, and said to her servant, Drive, and go forward; slack not thy riding for me, except I bid thee.
So she went and came unto the man of God to mount Carmel. And it came to pass, when the man of God saw her afar off, that he said to Gehazi his servant, Behold, yonder is that Shunammite:
Run now, I pray thee, to meet her, and say unto her, Is it well with thee? is it well with thy husband? is it well with the child? And she answered, It is well.

And when she came to the man of God to the hill, she caught him by the feet: but Gehazi came near to thrust her away. And the man of God said, Let her alone; for her soul is vexed within her: and the Lord hath hid it from me, and hath not told me.
Then she said, Did I desire a son of my lord? did I not say, Do not deceive me?

Then he said to Gehazi, Gird up thy loins, and take my staff in thine hand, and go thy way: if thou meet any man, salute him not; and if any salute thee, answer him not again: and lay my staff upon the face of the child.
And the mother of the child said, As the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. And he arose, and followed her.
And when Elisha was come into the house, behold, the child was dead, and laid upon his bed.
He went in therefore, and shut the door upon them twain, and prayed unto the Lord.

And he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands: and he stretched himself upon the child; and the flesh of the child waxed warm.
Then he returned, and walked in the house to and fro; and went up, and stretched himself upon him: and the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
And he called Gehazi, and said, Call this Shunammite. So he called her. And when she was come in unto him, he said, Take up thy son.
Then she went in, and fell at his feet, and bowed herself to the ground, and took up her son, and went out.

Then spake Elisha unto the woman, whose son he had restored to life, saying, Arise, and go thou and thine household, and sojourn wheresoever thou canst sojourn: for the Lord hath called for a famine; and it shall also come upon the land seven years.
And the woman arose, and did after the saying of the man of God: and she went with her household, and sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years.
And it came to pass at the seven years’ end, that the woman returned out of the land of the Philistines: and she went forth to cry unto the king for her house and for her land.
And the king talked with Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, Tell me, I pray thee, all the great things that Elisha hath done.

And it came to pass, as he was telling the king how he had restored a dead body to life, that, behold, the woman, whose son he had restored to life, cried to the king for her house and for her land. And Gehazi said, My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.

And when the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed unto her a certain officer, saying, Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.
Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:
Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
